name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,432

clue.text: Indeed — right time

blocks.note: yea is an old word for yes, indeed
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that the moment has come: yes, it is the right time.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is a fixed period on the calendar, so it is a unit or span of time.

clue.text: Interpreted thus, accountants voided capital

indicators.note: something voided has been emptied, so only the first and last letters of that word survive
read as inter-preted, the word suggests being placed between, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: the word with its middle emptied out leaves only its two end letters
then can mean thus or therefore, as in 'then it must be true'

explanation.surface: Bookkeepers are said to have emptied the capital's coffers, once the figures are interpreted that way.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a financial story; the capital is a city, and the small word thus is buried between the ends of accountants.
explanation.definitionFit: A capital is the seat of a nation's government, and the Greek government sits in this city.

clue.text: Party girl stifling smell about to grab male

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for smell runs backwards
to grab is to hold something within, so the male goes inside
stifling smothers what it holds, so the girl's name wraps around everything else

blocks.note: a common girl's name
reek is a strong unpleasant smell
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A party girl puts up with a nasty smell while grabbing a man.
explanation.walkthrough: KEER (reek turned round) takes M inside to make KEMER, which then sits inside MA-RY.
explanation.definitionFit: To make merry is a phrasal verb for celebrating, which is what partying means as a verb.

clue.text: Ripped off official, having looked around

indicators.note: around means the second word encircles the first

blocks.note: an ump is an umpire, an official in sport
gazed means looked steadily

explanation.surface: A referee feels cheated after having had a good look about.
explanation.walkthrough: Gazumping is British slang from house buying: a seller accepts a higher offer after agreeing a price with you.
explanation.definitionFit: Being gazumped means being cheated out of a purchase by a late higher bid, a form of being swindled.

clue.text: Threw away black stone I'd damaged

indicators.note: damaged letters are knocked out of shape, so they must be rearranged

blocks.note: jet is a deep black colour, as in jet-black
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone discarded a dark gem because it had been chipped.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw cargo or anything unwanted overboard, so jettisoned is the past tense for discarded.

clue.text: Possibly fool sporting body for nothing

blocks.note: a fool is a fruit-and-cream pudding, so possibly one example of a sweet
the FA is the Football Association

explanation.surface: An idiot plays for a sports team and is paid zilch.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweet FA is British slang for nothing at all; a fool here is the dessert, and in Britain a sweet is a pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet FA is a coarse British idiom meaning absolutely nothing, a euphemism for a ruder phrase.

clue.text: Moderate son getting a great deal

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
often means a great deal, frequently

explanation.surface: A restrained son lands a terrific bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: Moderate is the verb here, to tone down, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To soften something is to make it less harsh, which is what moderating it means.

clue.text: Local hyenas intermittently entering ground emptied in clearance

indicators.note: intermittently means on and off, so every other letter of the phrase is taken
emptied means the inside is removed, so only the two end letters remain
entering means going inside, so the first group of letters goes into the second

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on across both words
just the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Neighbourhood hyenas keep wandering onto cleared land.
explanation.walkthrough: The alternate letters run across both words, Local and hyenas, which the surface keeps apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The go-ahead is permission to proceed, and clearance is official approval to do something.

clue.text: Facile drivel mostly rejected

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the last letter is cut off
rejected suggests thrown back, so the letters are read in the other direction

blocks.note: bilge is slang for nonsense

explanation.surface: Superficial nonsense is largely dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: Glib and facile both describe speech that is fluent but shallow and lacking thought.

clue.text: Fancy — disheartened squirrels trapped in their nest

indicators.note: losing its heart means everything but the two outside letters goes
trapped in means held inside something else

blocks.note: a drey is the nest of a squirrel
only the two end letters of the word are kept

explanation.surface: An elaborate scene: dejected squirrels stuck in their home.
explanation.walkthrough: DREY is a word few solvers know outside crosswords: it is a squirrel's nest of twigs and leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressy clothes are smart and elaborate, and fancy as an adjective means ornate or elegant.

clue.text: Wanting to have church police

blocks.note: if you are for something you want it, as in all for it
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone longs for the church to have its own police.
explanation.definitionFit: The police are often called the force, as in a regional police force.

clue.text: Form one question in English exam, dropping second half of another

indicators.note: in places one group of letters inside another word
dropping the second half means only the first part of the word is kept

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a test is an exam
Roman numeral one
QU is a standard abbreviation for question
another exam, a second test

explanation.surface: Instructions for a candidate in an English exam: answer one question and drop half of another.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is imperfect: the first exam must also lose its S, which nothing in the clue signals. Form here means correct social behaviour, not a document.
explanation.definitionFit: Good form means proper behaviour by convention, which is exactly what etiquette describes.

clue.text: Lacking cover, soldiers gathered in a group

indicators.note: with no cover the outside edges are gone, so the first and last letters of the phrase are removed

blocks.note: men is a common word for soldiers, as opposed to officers
massed means gathered together

explanation.surface: Troops with no protection huddle together.
explanation.walkthrough: The covering letters come off the whole phrase men massed, not each word separately.
explanation.definitionFit: En masse is French borrowed into English meaning all together, as one body.

clue.text: New and concerning example of no-one getting the runs

definitions.text: example of no-one getting the runs

blocks.note: maiden means first or new, as in a maiden voyage
over can mean about or concerning, as in a row over money

explanation.surface: A fresh, worrying case of nobody suffering from diarrhoea.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls; a maiden over is one in which the batsmen score no runs. The runs is also slang for diarrhoea.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden over is a cricket over from which no runs are scored, so nobody gets any runs.

clue.text: Jerks back sadomasochistic idiots

indicators.note: back means the whole string of letters is read from the end

blocks.note: S and M is a short form of sadomasochism
saps are gullible fools

explanation.surface: Stupid people into S&M are a bunch of jerks.
explanation.walkthrough: Jerks looks like an insult for people, but here it is twitches, a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Spasms are sudden involuntary muscle contractions, or jerks of the body.

clue.text: Stopping reckless canoeists

indicators.note: reckless suggests wild and uncontrolled, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Paddlers taking risks are told to pull up.
explanation.definitionFit: A cessation is a halt or ending, the act of stopping something.

clue.text: Big occasion deserving wild dancing

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move about and change places

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grand event that merits some energetic dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A silver wedding is the twenty-fifth anniversary of a marriage, a major celebration for a couple.

clue.text: Sketch given unusual title, oddly enough

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so these letters come in an odd order
oddly here means taking the first, third and fifth letters

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
the odd-numbered letters of the word

explanation.surface: A drawing is given a strange name, which is odd.
explanation.walkthrough: Given looks like a link word joining the sketch to its title; it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A vignette is a brief descriptive scene or small illustration, a kind of short sketch.

clue.text: Wife calm, having left slyboots

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
ease is a state of calm
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A wife stays serene after a crafty person walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: Left looks like a verb, someone departing, but it just gives L.
explanation.definitionFit: A weasel is a sly, untrustworthy person, and a slyboots is someone cunning.

clue.text: Send out Henry to cut a flower

indicators.note: to cut into something is to go inside it

blocks.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Exe is a river in Devon
Hal is a pet form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal

explanation.surface: A man named Henry is sent to snip a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Flower is crossword code for river; the Exe is a river in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhale is to breathe out, sending air out of the lungs.

clue.text: Generally good for all not to open zip

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one piece swaps in where the other stood
with no opening, the first letter of the result is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good
taken as written, the letters being replaced

explanation.surface: Something that is usually beneficial for everyone is kept closed, like a zip.
explanation.walkthrough: G replaces ALL in GENERALLY to give GENERGY, then the first letter goes. Zip is the noun meaning vigour, not the fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: Zip is informal for liveliness or vigour, which is a sense of energy.

clue.text: To cover floors, picked up fabric

indicators.note: picked up as in heard, so the words are judged by their sound

blocks.note: to span is to cover a distance, and decks are the floors of a ship

explanation.surface: A material is chosen for carpeting the floors.
explanation.walkthrough: To cover floors becomes spanned decks, read in the past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Spandex is a stretchy synthetic fibre and the cloth made from it, also called Lycra or elastane.

clue.text: Dignified, posh adult returned unfinished relish

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the pair is read in the other direction
unfinished means without its end, so the last letter is cut

blocks.note: U means upper class, as in U and non-U
A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film ratings
gusto is hearty enjoyment

explanation.surface: A dignified, upper-class grown-up sends back a half-eaten condiment.
explanation.walkthrough: Relish looks like a pickle or sauce, but it means enjoyment here.
explanation.definitionFit: August as an adjective, stressed on the second syllable, means venerable and inspiring respect.

clue.text: It's not that things will turn out no good

indicators.note: to turn out is to expel, so the letters named are thrown out of the word

blocks.note: taken as written
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A grim prediction: matters will end up badly.
explanation.walkthrough: It's not that is a playful definition: this is the opposite of that.
explanation.definitionFit: This and that are paired pointing words, so this is the one that is not that.

clue.text: She sings to 2 clubs when touring

indicators.note: touring means travelling round, so the letters move about

blocks.note: taken as written
the answer to 2 down
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A singer performs in Greece and in nightclubs while on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: She sings suggests a female vocalist; it is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The stonechat is a small European songbird, so it is a creature that sings.

clue.text: Section of programme guide about this girl

indicators.note: a section is a part of the words that follow, so the letters lie inside them
about means turned round, so the concealed letters are read backwards

blocks.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Part of a TV listings magazine is about a particular girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemma is a girl's first name, so this answer is a particular girl.

clue.text: Regard standard record brand

blocks.note: to take note of
a level, as in up to the ...
to note down, as in ... a register
a trade name, as in a car marque or a branded ...

explanation.walkthrough: Four separate meanings of the one short word are strung together, with no wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark works as a verb for heeding and recording and as a noun for a level and a sign of identity.

clue.text: Classical father leers at bum

indicators.note: bum as an adjective means poor or faulty, so the letters come out wrong

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned dad ogles someone's behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Bum looks like a noun for bottom, but it is an adjective meaning bad.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Laertes is the father of Odysseus, a figure from classical literature.

clue.text: Watch start of court proceedings on outside broadcast

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the court piece follows the broadcast abbreviation

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for an outside broadcast
in tennis each point on court begins with a serve

explanation.surface: A viewer follows the opening of a trial on a live outside broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Court proceedings suggests a trial, but the court is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to watch carefully or keep an eye on something.
